\begin{bankq}[id=SI18-P2-PHY-S3-Q02, source={Score-I - Test 18 (24 Apr 2022)}, paper=2, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Calorimetry}, answer={3}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: final temperature when two solid argon samples, C proportional to T^3 are mixed | steps: energy of heating dU = integral of C dT = C0 T^4/(4 T0^3); conserve total U: m1 T1^4 + m2 T2^4 = (m1 + m2) Tf^4; masses 40 and 600 g; Tf = ((40 x 9^4 + 600 x 1)/640)^{1/4} = 5}]

One mole (40 g) of solid argon at temperature 8K is brought into thermal contact with two kilograms of solid argon at a temperature of 1K and they insulated everything together. What will be the temperature (in K) of the substance when thermal equilibrium is established? Round off to nearest integer.
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SI31-P2-PHY-S2-Q05, source={Score-I - Test 31 (29 Dec 2022)}, paper=2, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Calorimetry}, answer={60}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: time to melt equal ice quantities, heaters at different voltages | steps: power V^2/R for each element; time to melt = m L/P inversely proportional to V^2; ratio of times for the three containers; compute asked}]
Three identical containers, 1, 2 and 3, are filled with equal quantities of ice at $0^\circ$C and placed outside. Identical heating elements are placed inside each container. The elements are powered by different voltages: $V_1=380$ V, $V_2=220$ V, and $V_3=180$ V. In container 1, all ice melted in $t_1=4$ min. In container 2, all ice melted in $t_2=20$ min. How long (in minute) would it take to melt all the ice in container 3? Assume that the resistance of the heating elements remains constant and that the temperature of each container is constant throughout its volume at any given instant. Also assume the rate of heat loss to the surrounding is same for all three containers.
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA30-P1-PHY-S2-Q06, source={Score Advanced - Test 30 (04 May 2024)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Calorimetry}, answer={A,B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K1 S3 I1 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: nichrome wires in communicating vessels carrying current: heating  liquid | steps: wire heating rate I^2 R; liquid levels in two vessels; heat transfer to the liquid; change in level due to temperature or volume; compare the two vessels; compute | C: energy balance with Joule heating in two connected vessels}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 31 (04 May 2024) P1 Q6}]
Two identical thin homogeneous nichrome wires are mounted into the side non-conducting walls of vertical communicating vessels (vessel cross-sectional area S = 100 cm$^2$ and 3S). The vessels are filled upto a level 50 cm and covered with light and thin conductive pistons. The pistons do not allow water to pass through, have contact with the wires and can move without friction inside the vessels without leaving them, thanks to stoppers.\par
An ammeter is connected to the pistons using flexible wires (the length of the wires allows the pistons to move freely). The installation diagram is shown in the figure. When a non-conducting weight weighing 1 kg is placed on a small piston, the ammeter shows a current strength of $I_1$ = 2.31 A. If 3 such weights are placed on a large piston, the ammeter shows a current strength of $I_2$ = 2.1 A.\par

\opt{D}{The minimum current through the ammeter is approx. 1.5 A.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SA33-P2-PHY-S3-Q06, source={Score Advanced - Test 33 (12 May 2024)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=numerical, subtopic={Expansion}, answer={3}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: thermal expansion so that a brass ring slides onto a steel rod | steps: ring diameter 3.992 at 30 C expands with alpha_brass; rod 4.000 expands with alpha_steel; equate diameters d_ring (1 + a_b (T - 30)) = d_rod (1 + a_s (T - 30)); solve T | I: both diameters expand linearly with temperature}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 34 (12 May 2024) P2 Q6}]

\begin{bankq}[id=SA38-P1-PHY-S4-Q01, source={Score Advanced - Test 38 (13 Apr 2025)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=numerical, subtopic={Specific and latent heat}, answer={275}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S1 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: heat required, temperature dependent specific heat C = kT | steps: Q = integral of k T dT per kg from 250 K to 300 K = k (300^2 - 250^2)/2 = 13750 k; n = 13750 and n/50 = 275}]

\begin{bankq}[id=SA40-P2-PHY-S4-Q05, source={Score Advanced - Test 40 (27 Apr 2025)}, paper=2, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Specific and latent heat}, answer={5}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: final temperature when two solid argon samples, C proportional to T^3 are mixed | steps: energy of heating dU = integral of C dT = C0 T^4/(4 T0^3); conserve total U: m1 T1^4 + m2 T2^4 = (m1 + m2) Tf^4; masses 40 and 600 g; Tf = ((40 x 9^4 + 600 x 1)/640)^{1/4} = 5}]

\begin{bankq}[id=PS03-P1-PHY-S1-Q04, source={Pre-Score (2023-24) - Test 03 (22 Oct 2023)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=single, subtopic={Calorimetry}, answer={D}, answer_src=key, working={Printed key.}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: melting ice in boxes with heater power on different ice masses | steps: heater power equals heat absorbed plus heat lost through the wall; box lost heat depends on temperature difference at the outside; compare melting times for three boxes | I: lost heat through non insulated boxes makes the time depend on outside conditions | C: combining the given data for the comparison}]
On a cold winter's day, there are three identical, non-insulated wooden boxes in front of the house, each filled with the same amount of ice at a temperature of 0.0 $^\circ$C. To melt the ice, an electric heating element is placed in each of the boxes. The heating elements are identical, but are operated with different voltages. In the first box, the heating element is operated with a voltage of 80 V. All of the ice in the box will then melt in 20.0 minutes. A voltage of 120 V is applied to the heating element of the second box, whereupon the ice completely melts in just 4.0 minutes. In the third box, a voltage of 40 V is used for the heating element. The heating elements are designed in such a way that they heat the entire mass of ice in the respective box at the same time. Assume that the meltwater is not being heated by the heating element. \opt{B}{It takes about 100 minutes to melt all of the ice in the third box.}

\opt{D}{With the voltage used, it is not possible to melt all of the ice.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
